subject: [PATCH 1/3] blk-iolatency: clear delay state when freeing policy data

2026-08-06.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the blk-iolatency io controller where policy data is not properly cleared when it's freed, leading to incorrect throttling behavior. When a group has no latency target of its own, it can be throttled by its siblings, and if a peer reaches queue depth one, it gets stuck with a delay state even after the policy data is reset. The patch clears this delay state in the iolatency_pd_free function to prevent incorrect throttling behavior. This fix addresses an issue introduced in commit d70675121546.

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary: Raised a question about when blkg can be NULL in the iolatency_pd_free() function, and whether it's necessary to keep a guard against this case.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Aug 06, 2026 at 11:37:18AM -0700, Usama Arif wrote:
>  static void iolatency_pd_free(struct blkg_policy_data *pd)
>  {
> +	struct blkcg_gq *blkg = pd_to_blkg(pd);
> +
> +	/*
> +	 * Groups throttled as collateral have min_lat_nsec == 0, so
> +	 * iolatency_pd_offline() leaves their delay set.  Drop it here, where
> +	 * no in-flight bio can re-arm it via check_scale_change().
> +	 */
> +	if (blkg)

When can blkg be NULL here?

Thanks.

-- 
tejun

2026-08-10.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue in the blk-iolatency io controller where the delay state is not properly cleared when freeing policy data, leading to incorrect congestion counting and throttling of tasks. The fix involves adding a call to blkcg_clear_delay() in the iolatency_pd_free() function to clear the delay state.

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Clarified that blkg is only set when the pd is attached to a blkg, and that in the normal case it's not possible for blkg to be NULL.
reviews.raw_body:
On 10/08/2026 19:48, Tejun Heo wrote:
> On Thu, Aug 06, 2026 at 11:37:18AM -0700, Usama Arif wrote:
>>  static void iolatency_pd_free(struct blkg_policy_data *pd)
>>  {
>> +	struct blkcg_gq *blkg = pd_to_blkg(pd);
>> +
>> +	/*
>> +	 * Groups throttled as collateral have min_lat_nsec == 0, so
>> +	 * iolatency_pd_offline() leaves their delay set.  Drop it here, where
>> +	 * no in-flight bio can re-arm it via check_scale_change().
>> +	 */
>> +	if (blkg)
> 
> When can blkg be NULL here?
> 
> Thanks.
> 

Not in the normal case.

pd->blkg is only set when the pd is attached to a blkg.
blkcg_activate_policy() pre-allocates one outside the queue_lock when the
GFP_NOWAIT allocation fails, and frees it through pd_free_fn() if it ends up
unused \u2014 both at the retry and at the out: label. That pd never had ->blkg assigned.
It reads as NULL rather than garbage because iolatency_pd_alloc() uses kzalloc_node().

Good to keep as a guard in this case?

2026-08-12.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue in the blk-iolatency io controller where the delay state is not properly cleared when freeing policy data, leading to incorrect congestion counting and throttling of tasks. The fix involves adding a call to blkcg_clear_delay() in the iolatency_pd_free() function to clear the delay state.
